top_story.headline: Campaigns tell the FEC an electronic filing outage made them miss 48-hour notice deadlines
top_story.dek: Two House challengers' Form 99 letters, filed October 30 and dated October 28, say the FEC's e-filing system was down when their Form 6 notices came due, days before Election Day.
paragraphs: Vega for Congress, the campaign of New York 15th District Democratic challenger Jose David Vega, sent a paper 48-hour notice dated October 28 by overnight delivery and fax. It reports a $1,000 contribution received October 27 from Mario Vella of Wesley Chapel, Florida. Treasurer Adrian Spector Pearl wrote that the committee is a mandatory electronic filer and that the FEC's system, including the Form 6 webform, 'remains offline.' The letter encloses an FEC notice dated October 27 listing Form 1, Form 2, Form 5, Form 6, Form 9, Form 24 and Form 99 among the services that were down. That notice says the Commission may decline to pursue administrative fines against filers kept from filing by unforeseen circumstances, if they file within 24 hours after the circumstances end (11 CFR 111.35).

Eisenhauer for Congress, the campaign of Montana independent challenger Michael D. Eisenhauer, told the FEC in a one-line Form 99 that two Form 6 submissions dated October 26 and October 29 were late because the filing system was down, and that both were submitted October 30. The Form 99 itself carries an electronic image stamp of October 30 at 2:35 pm.
Neither filing shows when the outage ended or whether the FEC accepted the paper notice. Election Day is November 3, so late-contribution notices are at their densest.

sections.headline: Two sitting House members filed miscellaneous submissions
paragraphs: One is a new-looking committee registration form and one is a short amendment note. Neither raises a red flag.

items: Rep. Mark Pocan (D-WI) files a Form 1 statement of organization for Mark Pocan for Congress. The scan is rough, but it appears to name Sondy Pope as treasurer, list the University of Wisconsin Credit Union in Madison as the committee's bank and identify the committee as Pocan's principal campaign committee. The box marking it new or amended could not be read. Received 10/29. (Filing)

Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) tells the FEC that Self for Congress is amending a prior report to add a contribution from Globe Life PAC. The note cites the original filing as FEC-2044222 and gives no amount. Received 10/30. (Form 99)

sections.headline: No new RFAI letters in this window
paragraphs: No new RFAI letters surfaced in this window. Four of the Form 99s below are replies to earlier RFAIs.

sections.headline: Thirteen Form 99s: replies to FEC letters, new committee registrations and a candidate repaying himself
paragraphs: Four are replies to FEC information requests or letters (Boren, Democratic Socialists of America, Los Angeles County Democratic Central Committee, Wanda James). Three are Form 1 organization statements filed under Form 99 (Amalgamated Bank PAC, Gun Rights America, Kiros for Congress). The rest include two filings tied to the FEC e-filing outage (Vega, Eisenhauer), a loan forgiveness letter and a termination companion letter in which the candidate repaid himself. The Mandel letter is the one worth reading closely.

items: David Mandel for Congress 2024 tells the FEC that candidate David Mandel moved the campaign's remaining $11,000-plus to himself as partial repayment of loans he says total nearly $50,000. Mandel, a California Democratic challenger, writes that his former treasurer stopped responding, that earlier quarterly reports wrongly showed negative cash on hand, and that re-created data files showed only $20,000 in personal loans. He then closed the account and filed a termination on October 9. Filed 10/30. (Form 99)

Boren for Congress is told by former Rep. Dan Boren that printing and compliance consulting costs were campaign related and the committee will not be redesignated. Boren's October 22 letter to the FEC's Reports Analysis Division replies to a question about the April and July quarterly reports. He says he may run again and will not convert to a multicandidate committee. Boren, an Oklahoma Democrat, was in Congress from 2005 to 2013. Filed 10/30. (Form 99)

Wanda James for Congress tells the FEC it refunded all nine general-election contributions totaling $6,750 on July 29. The reply to the September 24 RFAI argues that the refunds fell outside the July Quarterly Report period because June 30, the Colorado primary date, was also the close of books. They appear on the October Quarterly Report. The letter says no amendment is needed and suggests the FEC review whether activity falls in a report period before sending such requests. Filed 10/29. (Form 99)

Democratic Socialists of America, Inc. tells the FEC it meant to file a Form 7 and resubmitted its report as a new entity by certified mail on October 13. The reply is to an RFAI dated October 5 about the July Quarterly Report (April 1 to June 30, 2026), addressed to analyst Bradley Austin. Filed 10/30. (Form 99)

Los Angeles County Democratic Central Committee tells the FEC that every payroll tax and salary payment on its report was for employees spending 25% or less of their time on federal election activity. The reply is to an RFAI dated September 24, and it adds that no employee spent more than 25% of their time on federal activity. Filed 10/29. (Form 99)

Lorita Daniels for US Senate tells the FEC that a $47,131 candidate loan has been forgiven. Candidate Lorita Daniels, a Virginia Democratic challenger, says a $3,480 refund from the Virginia Department of Education arrived after the termination report (April 1 to July 10, 2026) and was used to repay part of the loan. Filed 10/30. (Filing)
Vega for Congress files a paper 48-hour notice for a $1,000 contribution, saying the FEC's electronic filing system was offline. See the Top Story. Filed 10/30, letter dated 10/28. (Form 99)
Eisenhauer for Congress tells the FEC two Form 6 notices dated October 26 and October 29 were late because the filing system was down. Both were submitted October 30. See the Top Story. (Form 99)

Working America asks the FEC to change the email address on file for its independent expenditure filer account to Tcheng@workingamerica.org. The email says the group cannot access the email account tied to the filing entity, C90011156. Received 10/29. (Form 99)

Amalgamated Bank PAC files a Form 1 statement of organization listing Amalgamated Bank as its connected organization and Sam Brown as treasurer. The scan shows the committee, the connected organization and the committee's depository all at 275 Seventh Avenue in New York. Received 10/29. (Form 99)

Gun Rights America files a Form 1 statement of organization naming Benjamin Gates as treasurer. The Loveland, Colorado, committee lists First Advantage Bank in Fort Collins and First Community Bank in Lexington as depositories. Received 10/29. (Form 99)

Kiros for Congress files a Form 1 statement of organization naming Howie Stanger as treasurer. The committee backs Melat Kiros, a Colorado Democratic challenger, and lists Community Banks of Colorado, FirstBank, Amalgamated Bank and Ramp as depositories. The page header carries a 2025 date stamp. Received 10/29. (Form 99)

Committee to Elect Shane Bruce President tells the FEC its campaign has not reached the threshold that triggers reporting. The one-line note says the campaign has 'yet to reach the standard amount' for any reporting purposes. Filed 10/30. (Form 99)

sections.headline: Two large negative entries at a House campaign that also took a $1.3 million self-gift
paragraphs: Three new rows total about $304,600 in negative amounts. A negative figure is FEC's convention for a voided, reversed or refunded transaction and is usually mundane. The two Carbonara For Congress entries are large and involve a crypto wallet, and no description was given for either.

items: A $224,085.33 receipt from Ibanera BTC Crypto Wallet to Carbonara For Congress was reversed. The negative Schedule A entry is dated 5/6/2026 and has no description. (Filing)
A second $70,541.59 receipt from Ibanera BTC Crypto Wallet to Carbonara For Congress was reversed. The negative Schedule A entry is dated 6/8/2026 and has no description. (Filing)

A $10,000 contribution from S. Javaid Anwar to the California Republican Party Federal Account was reversed. The negative Schedule A entry is dated 9/22/2026, and its memo, which begins 'filer's % of contribution given to join…', is cut off in the record. (Filing)

A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.
